Description: 'An EF3 tornado near St. Libory, Nebraska captured and intercepted during a NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory storm chase project.' Original source given on Commons: Sean Waugh's post on X (https://x.com/MesonetMan/status/2056153136310411762).
title: Sean Waugh NOAA NSSL - Saint Libory Nebraska EF3 Tornado 17 05 2026
place: North of St. Libory, Howard County, Nebraska, USA
audio: original field audio from the moving vehicle (wind/road noise, possibly the crew talking); not checked by ear, mute it
notes: Handheld from a moving vehicle, so there is some shake and motion blur in the foreground field. 0-4 s: large, wide cone tornado on the horizon over green fields, tornado at x~0.35. 4-9 s: closer, condensation funnel fills the left-centre of the frame (x~0.3-0.4); around 7-8 s a tiny distant car drives on the gravel road under the tornado (not identifiable). 9-14 s: biggest and most dramatic, the wide tornado over a ploughed field, x~0.35-0.45, with a power line crossing at top right near the very end. Best seconds: 9-14 (fills the frame), then 3-8. Source 1280x720 (phone video), upscaled to 1920x1080 at 30 fps. No faces, no text, no logos. NWS survey: 0 fatalities, 0 injuries, but four homes were destroyed; none of that damage is visible in this clip.
fact_en: NWS Hastings survey of the Saint Libory tornado: 'Rating: EF-3', 'Estimated Peak Wind: 160 mph', 'Path Length /statute/: 6.09 miles', 'Path Width /maximum/: 350 yards', 'Fatalities: 0', 'Injuries: 0'.
